hero.eyebrow: Problems we are set up to solve
hero.title: Look at the engineering problem before prescribing the project.
hero.intro: The scenarios below show how SDK approaches technically consequential situations. They describe capabilities and decision paths, not invented client case studies or unsupported results.

scenarios.heading: Recognize the pressure. Then find the responsible first move.
scenarios.intro: A useful response connects business exposure to technical evidence and a decision the organization can act on.

items.title: The system is too important to replace blindly—and too costly to leave alone.
items.situation: Delivery slows as dependencies age, knowledge narrows and every change reaches further than expected.
questions: What must remain available during change?

items.title: The platform is under pressure, but capacity may not be the real problem.
items.situation: Latency, incidents or infrastructure cost are increasing and the available signals do not explain why.
signals: Recovery depends on a few people
questions: Where does time and capacity go?
What evidence is missing during incidents?

items.title: The AI demo works. The operating model around it does not exist yet.
items.situation: A promising model interaction must become a controlled workflow with trusted data, evaluation and human responsibility.
questions: How will quality be measured over time?

items.title: The product needs focused engineering ownership for a critical phase.
items.situation: The internal team has a defined priority but lacks one or more disciplines needed to carry the workstream safely.
signals: A critical roadmap item remains blocked
questions: Where do client decisions remain essential?

principle.heading: A portfolio is only persuasive when the evidence is real.
principle.body: SDK will publish named clients, quantified outcomes and testimonials only when the work, result and permission can be verified. Until then, this page shows the situations we are equipped to investigate and the deliverables that move them forward.

fit.heading: The strongest work starts with access, responsibility and a real decision to make.
fit.intro: Technical difficulty is welcome. An engagement becomes ineffective when the organization cannot provide context, access or decision ownership.
fitItems: A material software, data, AI or infrastructure constraint
Access to the system and people who understand its current state
A decision-maker who can resolve scope and trade-offs
Willingness to examine evidence before committing to a solution
notFitItems: Anonymous ticket capacity with no owned outcome
A request to validate a predetermined answer regardless of evidence
No practical access to the relevant system or stakeholders
Selection based only on the lowest individual day rate

cta.title: Start with what the system is costing, delaying or putting at risk.
cta.body: You do not need to diagnose it before contacting SDK. Tell us what is happening and which decision is currently blocked.
cta.label: Discuss the situation
